newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh taka ends flat, loses early edge.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh taka ends flat, loses early edge.

text.p: The Bangladesh taka surrendered early gains made in response to an easing in call rates and closed flat in a dull session on Wednesday, dealers said.
The local unit was quoted firmer at 42.8000/8200 per dollar in early trade but lost as call money rates fell by mid-day.
Call money was quoted at 9.5 to 10.5 percent in early trade on apprehension that payments against central bank bills worth 3.6 billion taka could cause a liquidity shortfall.
Call rates eased later and closed at 7.5 to 8.5 percent, against Tuesday's 7.75-8.5 percent, following simultaneous maturity of some old bills of the central bank, dealers said.
